# T7.01: full-range input signalled in the VUI

`EncConfig.full_range` writes `video_full_range_flag` into the H.264 and HEVC VUI, but `libnvencvt` never set it, so a
full-range input (`420f`, as Parsec and OBS with "Color Range: Full" deliver) was encoded as is and labelled video range:
decoders expanded 0..255 again (crushed blacks and whites, more contrast).

Now the range follows the session's first frame: `420f` / `xf20` are encoded as they are and signalled full range; `420v`
/ `x420` are video range; BGRA and l10r are converted by us to video range. The encoder log line says `range full|video`.

## Checked

- ffmpeg (`h264_videotoolbox` / `hevc_videotoolbox`, libnvencvt injected), 1280x720 testsrc2 through ffv1:
  full-range NV12 in -> streams `yuvj420p(pc, bt709)`, decoded Y 16..227 vs source 16..226 (full-range values);
  video-range in -> `yuv420p(tv, bt709)`, decoded 30..211 vs source 30..210.
- OBS 32.2.2 (`vm/tahoe/obs-rec.sh`, `OBS_RANGE=Full|Partial`): HEVC recordings `yuv420p(pc, bt709)` and
  `yuv420p(tv, bt709)`, 0 decode errors.
